exposure: Human milk composition (energy, macronutrients, free amino acids, inflammatory markers, hormones)
outcome: Infant gut microbiome diversity and composition (phylum, family, and genus)
cohort: 54 mother-infant pairs (infants were 51.9% male) at 6 months of age, with mothers exclusively breastfeeding
finding: Higher levels of interleukin-8 (IL-8) in human milk were associated with increased infant gut microbiome diversity and specific bacterial taxa, suggesting a potential role for IL-8 in shaping the infant gut microbiome.
